title: API Reference
markdown:
The FastAPI surface lives in `openexecutive.api.main`, which mounts one router per topic. A shared-secret middleware gates every request via an `x-api-key` header, except `/health` and the `/webhook/*` callbacks (which carry their own verification). CORS is restricted to configured UI origins. The gate is off when `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` is unset — intended for local development only — so any internet-reachable deployment sets `OE_PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT`, and `create_app()` then refuses to boot without the secret rather than serving an unauthenticated API.

Endpoints grouped by router:

| Router | Key endpoints | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `POST /chat`, `POST /chat/stop` | SSE stream of a live Executive turn. The request body optionally carries `page_context` (route, page title, guide section id, and a form descriptor with current values) — sent only by the Ask OE side panel so the Executive can explain the current page or propose form values. When the Executive calls its `propose_form_values` tool, the stream emits a `form_patch` event (`{type, form_id, fields, rationale, iteration}`) that the panel applies into the on-screen form as highlighted suggestions; the user reviews and saves through the form's normal submit path. Each round of tool calls also emits an `activity` event (`{type, label, tool, iteration}`) naming what is running — progress only, forwarded verbatim and never persisted with the message, unlike an `action_taken` chip. A `session_id` in the body must be a chat the caller may use (the same ownership rule as `sessions`). If it isn't, the turn runs in a fresh chat instead, so nothing is written into someone else's session and the reply looks the same as for an unknown id. An unknown namespaced id (`slack:…`, `telegram:…` and so on) is ignored and a fresh chat is started, because those ids belong to the channel adapters and claiming one first would make the caller its owner. The client mints a `client_turn_id` and sends it with the turn; `POST /chat/stop` takes that id and halts the turn mid-flight, so the button is live from the moment Send is pressed rather than only once the first SSE byte arrives. A stopped turn emits a `stopped` event and then the usual `done` over the same still-open stream — never an `error` — and whatever streamed so far is persisted and flagged. The endpoint returns 404 both for an unknown id and for another caller's turn, so it cannot be used to probe which turns are live. An optional `memory_text` (1–2000 chars) is what peer memory records as the caller's words instead of `message` — the briefing handoffs send it because their seed quotes the Executive's own card; `POST /chat/upload` derives it from the typed text and filenames. Since it never reaches the transcript, the `chat_turn` audit row keeps it beside `message`. |
| `sessions` | `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{id}`, `GET /sessions/{id}/messages`, `DELETE /sessions/{id}`, `POST /sessions/{id}/messages/{message_id}/feedback`, `GET /sessions/{id}/followup` | List, read and delete saved chat sessions (assistant messages carry their row `id` and any `feedback`). The list is scoped to the caller. Every per-session route checks ownership, because session ids are guessable (`slack:dm:<user id>`, `telegram:<chat id>`): only the session's owner or the principal gets through, and a legacy row with no owner is the principal's alone. Anyone else gets the same 404 as for an unknown id, so the routes can't be used to find out which chats exist. The one other way in is having started the chat in this process (matched by Person id or verified email, so it survives the caller being added to the roster), which is how a caller the roster can't resolve keeps using their own chat. That record is in memory, so after a restart such an ownerless chat is refused for reads. The principal can continue someone else's ownerless chat without becoming its owner. Deleting a session also drops its in-memory copy, so a later turn naming that id starts fresh. The feedback route records 👍/👎 (`{"feedback": "up"|"down"|null}`) on one assistant reply; only the session's own caller or the principal may rate it. The rater is stored (`feedback_by_person_id`), and a 👎 on a reply to the rater's own message triggers a working-style pass for them (paced; see attunement). The chat stream's `done` event carries `message_id` for the persisted reply. The followup route returns `{"suggestion": string|null}` — one suggested next user message, written by the utility-fast model from the last few turns, that the chat composer shows as its greyed placeholder (Tab / → or the inline chip fills it in without sending). It is null unless the session ends on a persisted assistant reply, and null (uncached) when the model fails. Same ownership check as feedback; successful suggestions are cached in-process per (session, reply id). |
| `today` | `GET /today`, `GET /today/activity`, `GET /today/activity/daily` | Morning-brief aggregation, recent-action rail, and Pulse heartbeat heatmap (per-day activity counts). |
| `people` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH /people`, `POST /people/{id}/archive`, `GET /people/{id}/open-loops`, `POST /open-loops/{loop_id}/close`, `GET /people/{id}/outreach`, `GET\|PUT\|DELETE /people/{id}/attunement` | Roster CRUD and scope lookups. Archiving a person closes their open loops. The open-loop routes list what a person owes (soonest due first) and close one (`reason`: done / not_needed / cancelled) — both the principal's or the owner's only (403 otherwise, via `people.store.is_principal_or_self`). `/outreach` returns, per kind of proactive outreach over 30 days, `sent` / `replied` / `acted` / `ignored` / `pending` (voided DMs are excluded) — same access rule, checked before the person lookup so it can't probe which ids exist. `/attunement` reads, replaces (`rules`: up to 4 strings, or omitted to only set `locked`) or resets the person's working-style rules — same access rule, 404 for an archived person; `PUT` rejects a rule that is not purely about style with 422. Archiving a person also drops their working style. |
| `departments` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /departments`, `.../goals` | Department state and per-department goals. `PATCH /departments/{slug}` also takes `watched_entities` (≤50 names, `[]` clears) — the entities the research watch policy may add watches for and route to this department. A `cadences` spec that does not parse is rejected with a 422 (empty means no cadence). |
| `agents` | `GET /agents`, `GET /agents/models`, `GET /agents/models/options`, `PATCH /agents/{id}`, `POST /agents/{id}/test` | Specialist metadata and Council overrides. `/agents/models` is the flat model allowlist the PATCH validator uses; `/agents/models/options` returns the same ids in the same order, each tagged with `provider`, `provider_label`, `route` (`direct` / `openrouter` / `local`) and a display `label`, for the Council's Provider → Model picker. |
| `personas` | `GET\|PUT\|POST\|DELETE /personas` | Executive persona definitions. |
| `alerts` | `POST /alerts/{id}/ack`, `POST /alerts/bulk-ack`, `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen`, `POST /alerts/review` | Groom the briefing queue. `ack` (`read`/`ack`/`dismissed`, optional `mute_topic`) also teaches a watch-sourced alert's watch (`trust_score`); `bulk-ack` takes explicit `alert_ids` and/or `older_than_days` + `category` (exempt sources skipped); `reopen` is the Undo for a `resolved` / `expired` / `dismissed` alert (never `ack` or an artifact / decision row; back to `unread` with every review stamp cleared and its TTL anchor refreshed, so it is live again even if older than its TTL); `review` runs the Executive's relevance review on demand (ignores the interval; still honours `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED`, the per-pass caps, the single-flight lock and per-alert idempotency) and returns the move counts. `bulk-ack` caps ids at 500, needs `older_than_days >= 1`, and applies watch feedback per row; `mute_topic` must be one of the alert's tags or a scoped `external:` / `department:` pattern. Alerts still surface only through the briefing (`/today` reads the live view) — there is no list, prefs, mutes, or live-stream endpoint. |
| `artifacts` | `GET /artifacts`, `POST /artifacts/{id}/archive` | Browsable research/document artifacts. |
| `decisions` | `GET /decisions`, `POST /decisions/{id}/{approve,reject,cancel}`, `GET /audit/reliability` | Approval-gated decision instances (e.g. calendar bookings). A proposed booking is surfaced on the briefing as a companion alert; approve/reject/cancel here also clear that alert. Reviewed in the briefing — there is no separate proposals page. |
| `audit` | `GET /audit/logs`, `GET /audit/logs/{id}`, `GET /audit/sessions/{id}`, `GET /audit/usage`, `POST /audit/log` | Durable audit trail of side effects. `/audit/sessions/{id}` adds a per-session token cost summary; `/audit/usage` aggregates token usage and OpenRouter cost across all sessions (totals, by day, by model, and by source — the part of the system that made the calls — including server-side web-search counts). |
| `architecture` | `GET /architecture/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | This documentation surface. |
| `guide` | `GET /guide/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | Plain-language user-guide content surface — mirrors `architecture` (static, version-controlled files; no LLM on the serving path). |
| `health` | `GET /health`, `GET /health/honcho` | Liveness probes (unauthenticated). |
| `documents` | `POST\|GET\|DELETE /documents`, `GET /documents/{filename}` | Upload, list, view extracted text, and delete indexed company docs. Upload is keyed on the filename, so re-uploading a document replaces its chunks rather than duplicating them, and `DELETE` removes the rows as well as the file. `domain` must be one of the eight specialist domains or `general`; anything else is a 400 rather than a 200 that indexes where no specialist can retrieve. |
| `executive` | `GET /executive/status`, `POST /executive/pause`, `POST /executive/resume` | Operator pause switch for all autonomous work (scheduler, Gmail poller, workflow resumer); inbound chat and DMs stay live. Status returns `{paused, paused_at, paused_by, reason, held_actions}` — `held_actions` counts due `pending` rows that fire on resume. `pause` takes an optional `reason` (≤200 chars) and is idempotent (re-pausing keeps the original start and reason); `paused_by` is the UI proxy's `x-caller-email`, else `api`. Behind the shared-secret middleware — not `SCHEDULED_ADMIN_TOKEN`, which the UI cannot send. Any caller may pause; `resume` is principal-only (`is_principal_or_self`, 403 otherwise; open while no principal is rostered; a header-less caller resolves to the principal as in `chat`), and status carries `can_resume` for the viewer so the UI hides Resume from everyone else. |
| `scheduled` | `GET\|DELETE` scheduled actions (`?status=…&order=asc\|desc`) | Pending and fired scheduled actions; `order` flips the `run_at` sort (asc=soonest-first for the upcoming queue, desc=most-recent-first for terminal-status history). |
| `watchlist` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /watchlist`, `POST /watchlist/{slug}/approve`, `POST /watchlist/{slug}/decline` | External-monitoring watchlist + signals. Rows carry `origin` (`manual` \| `executive` \| `research` \| `research_proposed`); `approve` turns a research suggestion (`research_proposed`, `dry_run`) into a live watch, `decline` `{reason: not_relevant \| too_noisy \| wrong_source}` removes it and records the decline (or, for `too_noisy`, keeps it live at a high floor), both 409 unless the row is a pending suggestion; `DELETE ?reason=` on a research-origin row records the decline too. |
| `workflows` | `GET /workflows`, `POST /workflows/{name}/runs`, `GET\|POST\|PUT\|DELETE /workflows/custom`, `GET\|DELETE /workflows/custom/{name}/targets`, `POST /workflows/runs/{run_id}/decision`, `GET /workflows/tools/search?q=`, `GET /workflows/tools/describe?names=` | Workflow catalog, run management, and user-created (dynamic) workflow CRUD. Custom definitions come back with a server-managed `owner_person_id` (the creator — the web caller on `POST`, set on insert only; a client-sent value is ignored), who is asked to approve a workflow's first write to a new target. `GET /workflows/custom/{name}/targets` lists the targets its tool steps may write to without asking and `DELETE …/targets?value=` forgets one. `POST /workflows/runs/{run_id}/decision` with `{decision: "approve"|"reject"}` answers a run awaiting a yes/no sign-off from the web app — 403 unless the caller is the person it waits on or the principal, 409 if it isn't awaiting or needs a written reply — through the same `apply_resolution` a chat reply uses. Custom create/update also rejects (422) any action-step tool that does not resolve, and so does `POST /workflows/custom/{name}/activate` when turning a workflow **on** — that click is the approval for a tool workflow chat saved switched off (turning off is never checked). Turning on a workflow with action steps requires the body `{is_active: true, definition}` carrying the definition the user reviewed; if the stored one differs (ignoring `is_active` and timestamps) it returns 409, and the switch itself is a compare-and-set on the validated revision (`dynamic_store.activate_if_unchanged`, keyed on `updated_at`), so a save that lands while the tool check awaits the gateway — even from another process — is a 409 too, so only what was shown gets switched on. `GET /workflows/custom` lists inactive definitions too; `GET /workflows/{name}` 404s for them. The two `tools` endpoints return `{tools: [{name, description, read_only, source}]}` for the advanced editor's tool picker and the review card; `read_only` is true only when the name says it reads (a label, not a control). The run stream adds a `progress` event (`step_id`, `summary`) while an action step uses tools. Each catalog entry (`WorkflowMeta`) carries `is_custom` and `background` (true for the system-run built-ins the UI files under “System”). The run endpoint streams SSE; its `awaiting_human` event carries `delivery` (`self` \| `sent` \| `suppressed` \| `alerted` \| `failed`) alongside `person_id` / `question` / `awaiting_until`, because the outbound guard or an unreachable approver means the question may never have been asked — a client must not render “waiting on them” for those. A paused run ends the stream with neither `done` nor `error`, so that `awaiting_human` frame carries `terminal: true` to say so explicitly, plus `resumable` — whether the run continues by itself once answered or stops at the gate. `GET /workflows/runs/{run_id}` returns the run row with the resume payload replaced by a small `resume_progress` summary (`gate_step_id`, `completed_step_ids`, or `null`): the payload holds every completed step's full text, and the run-detail page polls this endpoint while a run is unfinished. |
| `knowledge` | `/knowledge/builtin`, `/external`, `/search` | MBA knowledge base and external sources. `/search` is the introspection parallel of `retriever.retrieve` and mirrors its filters — including the `general` catch-all on the company collection — so the panel cannot report a specialist seeing nothing that it does retrieve in chat. It accepts `general` in `domain_filter` for the same reason. `/search` applies the same review gate as `retrieve()` — withheld (pending or rejected) built-in, external and failure rows are dropped, so the panel never advertises knowledge the Executive cannot use; it degrades to unfiltered rather than failing if review state is unreadable. `POST /knowledge/builtin` refuses a name already held by shipped content, and `POST|DELETE /knowledge/failures` now register and deregister for review — without that a user-authored failure case study had no review row, so no SME decision could block it. |
| `skills` | `/skills`, `/skills/search` | Skill registry CRUD and search. |
| `evals` | `/evals/scenarios`, `/evals/runs` | Eval scenarios and run results. |
| `memories` | `/memories/{decisions,initiatives,advice}`, `GET /memories/people`, `GET /memories/people/{person_id}/conclusions` | Episodic-memory record management, plus the read-only peer-memory overview the Pulse People tab reads (`{status: ok|disabled|error, people: [...], conclusion_total}`; `?recent=` 1–50, default 5) and one person's full conclusion list, paged newest first (`{status, person_id, items, page, size, total, has_more}`; `?page=` ≥1, `?size=` 1–100, default 50; 404 when the person has no peer). |
| `review` | `/review/items`, `/review/stats`, `/review/trusted-defaults`, `POST /review/curate`, `POST /review/bulk-approve` | Knowledge review queue and annotations. Shipped knowledge registers as a trusted default (`approved` with a NULL `reviewed_at`), so the queue starts empty; `curate` (`{domain, action: start|stop}`, domain required) opts one domain in or out, and `trusted-defaults` returns domain → unreviewed count. `bulk-approve` takes a non-empty `domain`, `item_ids` (max 500) or `all_pending: true`, and 400s with no selector; it returns `{approved_count, item_ids}`. |
| `onboarding` | `/onboard/interview/start`, `/onboard/interview/message`, `/onboard/interview/draft`, `/onboard/interview/{id}`, `/onboard/interview/commit` | Conversational company setup. The `onboarding_interviewer` agent asks clarifying questions, then emits a draft profile + people + departments. **Nothing is persisted until `POST /onboard/interview/commit`** — the interview itself never writes. `start` is multipart (description + optional deck/one-pager uploads). |
| `workflow_designer` | `POST /workflows/designer/start`, `POST /workflows/designer/message`, `POST /workflows/designer/draft`, `GET /workflows/designer/{session_id}` | The conversational New workflow wizard. The `workflow_designer` agent asks clarifying questions (`phase: "question"`, with `hint` and up to four suggested `options`), then returns `phase: "draft"` with `draft.definition` (exactly the body `POST /workflows/custom` takes), `summary`, and `assumptions`; every response carries the `transcript`. **Nothing is persisted here** — sessions are in memory, and the UI saves through `POST /workflows/custom`. Errors are fixed strings (422 over the 8,000-char message cap or the transcript cap, 404 for an expired session, 409 while another turn on the same session is still running, 502/504 for model failure or timeout). Mounted ahead of the `workflows` router. |
| `onboarding` (fallback) | `/onboard/start`, `/onboard/answer`, `/onboard/status/{id}` | The original 12-step form wizard, kept as a fallback (UI at `/onboard?mode=form`) and used by the `openexecutive onboard` CLI. |
| `company-profile` | `GET\|PATCH /company-profile` | Structured company profile. |
| `auth` | `GET /auth/allowed-emails` | Non-archived people with an email, offered to the UI's sign-in gate. The gate takes the **union** of this roster and its own `ALLOWED_EMAILS` env list, so env entries always work (and are checked first, short-circuiting the fetch) and roster entries are additive — a roster change can never revoke a configured operator. |
| `fixtures` | `/fixtures`, `/fixtures/{name}/load` | Demo-company fixture load/reset/snapshot. |
| `clients` | `/clients`, `/clients/generate`, `/clients/cockpit`, `/clients/save`, `/clients/{slug}/activate` | Client-company slots — multi-client mode for fractional use; create from current/blank/AI-generated intake draft (pasted notes and/or file attachments, multipart on `/clients/generate`), save-back switching, engagement metadata (PATCH), cross-client cockpit, delete. See the Client Companies section. |
| webhooks | `POST /webhook/telegram`, `POST /webhook/google-chat` | Inbound integration callbacks (self-verified). |
| MCP server | `POST\|GET /mcp` | Open Executive exposed as an MCP server (Streamable-HTTP). Not a router — a mounted FastMCP sub-app. Same shared-secret gate (`x-api-key`); exposes company context as resources and the specialist council as tools. See the MCP Server section. |
